nodes.label: ADR-007: per-peer bearer token over TLS or WireGuard
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: per-peer bearer token over tls or wireguard
nodes.rationale: With two to five nodes and Tailscale as the trust boundary, a 32-byte per-peer token hashed at rest is simpler and more auditable than building a PKI; request signing with Ed25519 waits for H6.

nodes.label: Known implementation limitations (328 tests, two-PC test pending)
nodes.norm_label: known implementation limitations (328 tests, two-pc test pending)
nodes.rationale: The cut is deliberately declared incomplete: no lease renewal during execution, artifacts not packaged, ASK does not send, and no real two-PC Tailscale run yet. Documenting these prevents claiming isolation or completeness that does not exist.

nodes.label: permission.asked event blocks the prompt indefinitely
nodes.norm_label: permission.asked event blocks the prompt indefinitely

nodes.label: Permission broker (once or reject, never always)
nodes.norm_label: permission broker (once or reject, never always)

nodes.label: ADR-005: ODW brokers tool permissions and never answers always
nodes.norm_label: adr-005: odw brokers tool permissions and never answers always
nodes.rationale: In headless mode an unanswered permission.asked blocks forever, so ODW must answer; always would turn one command into a permanent grant, so only once or reject are allowed.

nodes.label: execution.succeeded does not mean task success
nodes.norm_label: execution.succeeded does not mean task success
nodes.rationale: A rejected tool permission produces session.tool.failed yet the turn still reports session.execution.succeeded, so completion must be derived from required evidence, not from the terminal event alone.

nodes.label: Approval binding to task_id, task_hash and nonce
nodes.norm_label: approval binding to task_id, task_hash and nonce

nodes.label: Approval channels: Telegram and named pipe
nodes.norm_label: approval channels: telegram and named pipe

nodes.label: ADR-009: approval only out of band, never over HTTP
nodes.norm_label: adr-009: approval only out of band, never over http
nodes.rationale: The agent must not be able to approve its own delegation, so approvals exist only via Telegram and an admin-only named pipe, are bound to task_id, task_hash and nonce, expire in 15 minutes and are single-use.

nodes.label: ADR-011: canonical task_hash via RFC 8785 JCS
nodes.norm_label: adr-011: canonical task_hash via rfc 8785 jcs
nodes.rationale: A canonical JSON projection plus SHA-256 makes the approval hash reproducible across languages and verifiable with test vectors, instead of depending on serialization order.

nodes.label: kind x workspace.mode compatibility matrix
nodes.rationale: code_change in read_only is rejected because a task that must modify files cannot run in a workspace with no write access; it prevents incoherent contracts.

nodes.label: Network isolation: WFP by SID plus CONNECT proxy
nodes.norm_label: network isolation: wfp by sid plus connect proxy

nodes.label: ADR-006: isolation by clone, not git worktree by default
nodes.norm_label: adr-006: isolation by clone, not git worktree by default
nodes.rationale: A worktree .git file points at the real repository outside the sandbox, so ACL isolation would be fictitious; a full local clone, or git archive for read-only, keeps the original repo out of reach.

nodes.label: ADR-012: repositories by logical name only
nodes.norm_label: adr-012: repositories by logical name only
nodes.rationale: The remote contract carries a logical repo name resolved by a local table, eliminating path traversal and disclosure of the disk topology; any absolute, UNC or .. path is rejected.

nodes.label: Two interfaces: local MCP facade and peer API
nodes.norm_label: two interfaces: local mcp facade and peer api

nodes.label: OpenCode SSE: data-only lines, no Last-Event-ID
nodes.norm_label: opencode sse: data-only lines, no last-event-id

nodes.norm_label: task event sse stream with resumable seq

nodes.label: Hybrid delegation: automatic only where a rule allows it
nodes.norm_label: hybrid delegation: automatic only where a rule allows it
nodes.rationale: Automatic delegation is limited to explicit AUTO rules; everything else needs human approval, balancing speed against the risk of an LLM granting itself remote execution.

nodes.label: No master node; symmetric bidirectional delegation
nodes.norm_label: no master node; symmetric bidirectional delegation
nodes.rationale: ODW must not introduce a coordinator role: any node can delegate and execute at the same time, so availability and capability are not concentrated in one PC.

nodes.label: ADR-002: two listeners, two ports, two authentications
nodes.norm_label: adr-002: two listeners, two ports, two authentications
nodes.rationale: Separating the local MCP facade from the peer API prevents a local agent from reaching the peer API and prevents the network from reaching MCP; startup refuses non-Tailscale peer binds and non-loopback MCP binds.

nodes.label: ADR-008: SQLite with a single writer and WAL
nodes.norm_label: adr-008: sqlite with a single writer and wal
nodes.rationale: Concurrent SQLite writers serialize and surface intermittent SQLITE_BUSY, so all writes go through one SqliteWriter actor with one transaction per command, while WAL keeps readers non-blocking.

nodes.label: ADR-010: one state per role in a single tasks table
nodes.norm_label: adr-010: one state per role in a single tasks table
nodes.rationale: Origin and target see different states for the same task_id; storing both with primary key (task_id, role) and two state machines over one enum avoids duplicating machines and ambiguous reconciliation.

nodes.label: OpenAPI spec served at GET /openapi.json, pinned by SHA-256
nodes.norm_label: openapi spec served at get /openapi.json, pinned by sha-256

nodes.label: Port 0 plus /api/info pid and urls discovery
nodes.norm_label: port 0 plus /api/info pid and urls discovery

nodes.label: OpenCode v2.3.2 V2 surface under /api (143 routes)
nodes.norm_label: opencode v2.3.2 v2 surface under /api (143 routes)

nodes.label: ADR-003: hand-written OpenCode client pinned by spec hash
nodes.norm_label: adr-003: hand-written opencode client pinned by spec hash
nodes.rationale: Code generators mishandle contentMediaType SSE bodies and x-effect-stream, so a small typed client is written by hand and the OpenAPI file is pinned by SHA-256, making drift fail a test instead of production.

nodes.label: ADR-004: one opencode serve instance per task
nodes.norm_label: adr-004: one opencode serve instance per task
nodes.rationale: A shared instance could leak sessions and permissions between tasks; one instance per task with an ephemeral port, random password and Job Object gives deterministic kill and state isolation.

nodes.label: ADR-001: target platform .NET 10 LTS
nodes.rationale: .NET 8 left support in November 2026 and .NET 11 is not LTS, so a long-lived service targets net10.0 with a pinned 10.0.x band.
